title: Interventions for managing immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps.
abstract: Immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps are difficult candidates for conventional root canal fillings. Interventions for management of such teeth include regenerative endodontic procedures (REPs), apexification, and root strengthening interventions. Basic principles involve removal of necrotic pulp, canal debridement and infection control. Currently, there is no evidence-based guidance to manage such teeth. title: World Health Organization non-laboratory-based 10-year cardiovascular disease risk prediction model in adults without established disease.
abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (prognosis). The objectives are as follows: The objective of this review is to evaluate the prognostic performance of the World Health Organization (WHO) non-laboratory-based CVD risk prediction models in adults aged 40 years to 74 years without established CVD. title: Curcuma longa (turmeric) or its active ingredients for osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a major cause of disability worldwide. Current treatments have limited efficacy. Curcuma longa (turmeric) contains curcuminoids with anti-inflammatory properties that may modulate osteoarthritis pathophysiology. However, the clinical benefits and safety of Curcuma longa in osteoarthritis remain uncertain. To assess the benefits and harms of Curcuma longa extracts or сurcuminoids for osteoarthritis. title: Low-dose oral misoprostol for induction of labour.
abstract: Oral misoprostol is a common labour induction method. This review is restricted to lower doses (initially ≤ 50 µg), as higher doses pose unacceptably high risks of uterine hyperstimulation. To assess the benefits and harms of low-dose oral misoprostol for labour induction in women with a viable fetus in the third trimester of pregnancy, compared with other methods of labour induction. We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO ICTRP, and checked reference lists…

title: Regimens of vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy.
abstract: Vitamin D deficiency is common in pregnancy and has been associated with adverse health outcomes for the mother and infant, including pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and low birthweight. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a vitamin D intake of 200 international units (IU) per day during pregnancy. Vitamin D supplementation is recommended for women with suspected vitamin D deficiency, but it is not universally recommended. The effects of different doses (regimens)…

title: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) for treating advanced epithelial ovarian cancer.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the eighth most common cancer in women worldwide. Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the most common type; three-quarters of cases present with advanced disease (stage III or IV). Treatment consists of combinations of surgery and chemotherapy. Although initial responses to chemotherapy are good, most women with advanced disease relapse. title: Chest physiotherapy for pneumonia in children.
abstract: Pneumonia is the single largest infectious cause of death in children aged under five years and remains a relevant cause of illness and death amongst older children and adolescents worldwide. Most pneumonia-related deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries, where access to healthcare resources, diagnostic services, and supportive treatments may be more limited than in high-income settings. title: Levothyroxine for subclinical hypothyroidism.
abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To evaluate the benefits and harms of levothyroxine for adults with subclinical hypothyroidism, compared with placebo or no treatment.

title: Living evidence map of the global climate and health literature.
abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (flexible). title: Levodopa or dopamine agonists for enhancing motor function after stroke.
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. There is a lack of evidence regarding pharmacological enhancement of stroke recovery with dopamine agonists or levodopa, in particular in terms of motor deficits. To assess the effects of dopaminergic agents, defined as levodopa or dopamine agonists, on improving motor function after stroke.
